narrative.overview:
Every design decision in this system originates from a single image: stepping into a beautifully lit room full of people who love each other. The Demarks 360 brand is the 360 booth at that party: warm, present, reliable, and genuinely delighted to be there. Joy is the first impression; trust is the aftertaste.

This is a Calgary family business, owned by a Muslim mother, and the design must reflect that grounded, community-first spirit. It is accessible to every family, every culture, every type of celebration. The warmth is not decorative. It is the product.

This system explicitly rejects: nightclub energy, corporate rental-catalog dryness, AI-generated SaaS aesthetics, and cold editorial luxury.
keyCharacteristics: Warm sand and charcoal surfaces, never pure white or pure black
Amber gold used as the one celebratory accent, not decoration
DM Serif Display italic for emotional emphasis; Nunito for everything readable
Rounded cards (16px) that feel soft rather than sharp
Sections alternate warm sand and warm charcoal for rhythm, never monotone

rules.name: The Warm Tint Rule
rules.body: No pure whites or pure blacks. Every surface is tinted toward amber. If a color passes the 'is this pure white?' or 'is this pure black?' test, it is wrong.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Event Amber appears on no more than 10% of any screen. It marks joy, emphasis, and the brand. It never fills a section background, a card, or a large button.

rules.name: The Two-Line Heading Rule
rules.body: Every display heading is a two-liner: one straight line in charcoal/sand, one italic amber line. The straight line states the fact; the italic amber line makes it feel.

rules.name: The Italic Accent Rule
rules.body: Italic in DM Serif Display is reserved for the amber-colored second line of display headings, the '360' in the logo, and hero copy <em> emphasis. Nowhere else.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. No card has a shadow in its resting state. Shadows appear only as hover state feedback.

dos: Do tint every surface toward amber. Use #EDE8DF (Warm Sand) as the lightest, #1A1714 (Celebration Charcoal) as the darkest.
Do use the two-line heading structure for every display heading: straight first line, italic amber second line.
Do keep Event Amber to 10% of any screen surface.
Do alternate sections: warm sand, charcoal, warm sand. The rhythm creates scroll momentum.
Do make booking effortless: price, CTA, and service area visible within the first two screens on mobile.
Do use rounded cards (16px) for all card containers.
donts: Don't use nightclub aesthetics: no neon, no aggressive all-caps heavy condensed fonts, no red/black high-contrast combos.
Don't use corporate event rental catalog aesthetics: no dry product grids, no emotionless pricing tables.
Don't produce AI-built SaaS landing page aesthetics: no purple or blue gradients, no glass cards on dark backgrounds, no hero metric grids.
Don't use cold editorial luxury: no all-Cormorant italic layouts, no fashion-magazine distance.
Don't use em dashes. Use commas, colons, semicolons, or periods instead.
Don't use border-left as a colored accent stripe greater than 1px on cards or list items.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient).
Don't add a resting-state shadow to any card. Shadows are hover-only.
Don't set all-caps body copy. Reserve uppercase for the 0.62rem section labels only.
